questions.q: Why is a Formula field read-only?
options: Because Salesforce disables editing on all calculated-looking fields
Because its value is computed fresh from other fields every time it's viewed, not stored or typed in
Because only System Administrators can view it
Because it is actually a Text field in disguise
questions.explain: A Formula field stores nothing — its value is recalculated from its source fields on every view, so there's nothing for a user to type into.

questions.q: What does the Insert Field tool in the formula editor let you do that's notable?
options: Only insert fields from the current object, never a related one
Insert a field reference, including fields on a related object reached across a relationship
Insert an image into the formula
Automatically fix syntax errors
questions.explain: Insert Field's picker can drill into a related object (like Account from an Opportunity), inserting correct cross-object syntax automatically.

options: Deletes the formula if it has an error
Validates the formula and surfaces errors (like a missing parenthesis) before you can save
Converts the formula field into a Roll-Up Summary field
Publishes the formula to all other objects
questions.explain: Check Syntax validates the formula and reports problems immediately, rather than letting an invalid formula reach save.

questions.q: In the real example AND(Account.NumberOfEmployees > 1000, Amount > 10000), what does the field return?
options: A number representing total employees
A True/False value, true only when both conditions hold at the same time
A list of account names
An error, because formulas cannot cross relationships
questions.explain: AND() returns true only when every argument inside it is true — here, the related Account's employee count exceeding 1000 and the Opportunity's own Amount exceeding 10000.

questions.q: What happens to a Formula field's displayed value if one of its source fields changes?
options: Nothing — it keeps showing the old value until manually recalculated
It reflects the new value automatically the next time the record is viewed
The field is deleted
The field becomes a Text field
questions.explain: Because a Formula field recalculates on every view rather than storing a value, it's never stale — a change to a source field shows up immediately on reload.
